items.lp_book_number: Successive Differences: the cubes up to 216
items.question_text: Find the successive differences of the cubes 1, 8, 27, 64, 125 and 216 until they are constant.
items.reason: The six cubes are written in the question text; the book's printed figure (P15-number_pattern-3: the row 1 8 27 64 125 216 with a curved arrow between neighbours) only repeats them and leaves every level blank, so the student needs no picture to attempt the question. The printed row and arrows are folded into the complete tower on the solution side (C95).

items.lp_book_number: Successive Differences: the cubes up to 216
items.question_text: Find the successive differences of the cubes 1, 8, 27, 64, 125 and 216 until they are constant.
items.reason: The book's own answer to 'compute successive differences over levels' is the filled difference tower (the book prints that structure for the squares); each difference sits between the two numbers it comes from and the equal row at level 3 is the finding. The LP steps give the numbers as text, but the arrangement is a filled figure, so it is drawn (B2: answer is an arrangement even when the steps describe it in words).

diagram.manim_description: Draw a difference tower on a 1920 by 1080 px canvas, background BG. Origin is the top-left corner; x grows to the right, y grows downward. Row labels in INK, 44 px, right-aligned at x = 330: 'Cubes' centred at y = 200, 'Level 1' at y = 410, 'Level 2' at y = 620, 'Level 3' at y = 830. Row 1 (y = 200), INK, bold, 60 px, six numbers centred at x = 450, 690, 930, 1170, 1410, 1650: 1, 8, 27, 64, 125, 216. Row 2 'Level 1' (y = 410), ANSWER, bold, 60 px, five numbers, each centred under the gap between the two cubes above it, at x = 570, 810, 1050, 1290, 1530: 7, 19, 37, 61, 91. Row 3 'Level 2' (y = 620), ANSWER, bold, 60 px, four numbers at x = 690, 930, 1170, 1410: 12, 18, 24, 30. Row 4 'Level 3' (y = 830), ANSWER, bold, 60 px, three numbers at x = 810, 1050, 1290: 6, 6, 6. Draw curved arrows in GUIDE, 3 px stroke, each an arc that dips 28 px below its row: under Row 1 five arcs, one from each cube to the next (1 to 8, 8 to 27, 27 to 64, 64 to 125, 125 to 216); under Row 2 four arcs (7 to 19, 19 to 37, 37 to 61, 61 to 91); under Row 3 three arcs (12 to 18, 18 to 24, 24 to 30). Each arc starts 20 px to the right of the centre of its first number and ends 20 px to the left of the centre of its next number, 50 px below that row's centre line, with the arrowhead at the right end pointing up to the next number. Draw no arcs under Row 4. Draw a dashed FOCUS rounded rectangle, 4 px stroke, around the three 6s, from x = 730 to x = 1370 and from y = 785 to y = 875. No other text, line or colour.
accuracy_checks: Row 1 holds the cubes 1^3 to 6^3: 1, 8, 27, 64, 125, 216 (six numbers)
Level 3: 18-12=6, 24-18=6, 30-24=6 (three equal numbers, so the differences are constant at level 3)
Each lower number is centred exactly midway between the two numbers above it that it is the difference of (x = 570 between 450 and 690, and so on)
diagram.alt_text: A difference tower: the cubes 1, 8, 27, 64, 125, 216, then Level 1 differences 7, 19, 37, 61, 91, Level 2 differences 12, 18, 24, 30 and Level 3 differences 6, 6, 6, with the equal 6s outlined.
diagram.render_note: The book prints only the top row with its arrows (P15-number_pattern-3) and leaves the levels blank, and the LP question names the six cubes, so the question has no diagram and this solution figure draws the whole tower itself (derived_from null). The book's coloured Level labels (red, blue) are replaced by the house tokens: given cubes INK, computed differences ANSWER. No '...' after 216 because the LP stops at 216.

items.question_text: Arrange 1 to 17 in a row so that each pair of neighbours adds to a perfect square.
items.reason: The book gives a row of 17 empty boxes to fill and the example's answer is exactly that filled row (an arrangement, B2); the finished row with its neighbour sums is the picture the example needs, while the empty boxes alone carry no information. The LP lists the arrangement and the 16 sums as text.

Cell centres run x = 128, 232, 336, ... in steps of 104 px up to x = 1792 for cell 17. Write INK, bold, 52 px numbers centred in the cells, left to right: 16, 9, 7, 2, 14, 11, 5, 4, 12, 13, 3, 6, 10, 15, 1, 8, 17. Cells 1 and 17 (the numbers 16 and 17) get a FOCUS outline of 6 px instead of the INK outline. Under every pair of neighbouring cells draw a small GUIDE bracket, 3 px stroke: it goes down 18 px from a point 8 px to the right of the left cell's centre, runs across to a point 8 px to the left of the right cell's centre, and goes up 18 px; the horizontal part of every bracket is at y = 548 and its ends are at y = 530.
